newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX volatilities soften as dlr bounces.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX volatilities soften as dlr bounces.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar-pair options softened in U.S. afternoon business as the greenback bounced off overnight lows, recouping some of the big losses in the past few days, dealers said.

The U.S. unit climbed back above an important psychological barrier of 1.5000 marks, helped by verbal support from Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer, but many traders saw the rebound and the ensuing pullback in volatilities as a corrective move.
"It's not so surprising to see spot come back a little bit because it fell a lot yesterday," said a U.S. bank trader.
While the spot dollar was more than a pfennig above early lows, its uptrend since late July has been severely damaged and the risk clearly seemed to be to the downside, he added.
Traders said Tietmeyer's comments contained little news.
Tietmeyer said the dollar was finding its way back up and that he always welcomed the dollar being at "correct levels."
Implied volatility for one-month dollar/mark options stood at 8.1/8.3 percent, off nearly half a point from late Monday highs.
The volatility curve was flat as traders stayed wary of selling down the back end.
Three-month, six-month and one-year were all pretty much around 8.2/8.4 percent.
Risk reversals, which compare pricing of puts and calls, were little changed, with one-month 25-delta at 0.3/0.7 percent in favor of mark calls.
Dollar/yen volatilities also eased as spot clawed back above 111.50 yen after dipping below 111.00 yen Monday.
"Whether we've seen the dollar's bullish trend reversed or we're just settling into a range remains an open question," said Masao Okada, chief option dealer at Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank in New York.
"But judging from the behavior of the market, it looks like a lot of people may be thinking dollar/yen is staying in the 110-115 yen range," he said.
"I don't think this latest down cycle in spot is over, but I'm starting to think it might be all right to sell some gamma for now because the front-end is relatively rich," he added.
Front-end options have higher gamma implications than longer-dated contracts, meaning they are more sensitive to spot market gyrations but more vulnerable to time decay.
One-month dollar/yen implied volatility stood at 8.2/8.4 percent, off more than a quarter point from late Monday.
The back end was stable, with one-year at 9.75/9.9 percent.
A large investment bank was seen aggressively bidding the four-month area, while the two-month area was soft as they cover a period when the market tends to be subdued.
One-month 25-delta dollar/yen risk-reversal narrowed slightly to 0.7/0.8 percent from 0.8/1.0 on Monday. It had widened sharply late last week from near-par levels.
